questions.question: According to the article, which work did Mozart write toward the end of his last Italian journey that remains a favorite for performance by sopranos today?
options: the solo motet Exsultate, jubilate, K. 165
the opera Mitridate, re di Ponto
the opera Ascanio in Alba
the opera Lucio Silla
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that toward the end of the last Italian journey, Mozart wrote the solo motet Exsultate, jubilate, K. 165, and that this work is a favorite for performance by sopranos today.
Incorrect. Mitridate, re di Ponto was written in Milan in 1770 and led to further commissions, but the article does not identify it as a soprano favorite from the end of the last Italian journey.
Incorrect. Ascanio in Alba was composed during a return visit to Milan in 1771, not at the end of the last Italian journey.
Incorrect. Lucio Silla was premiered in 1772 during a later Milan visit, not at the end of the last Italian journey.

questions.question: According to the article, what trend across time is noted in Stafford (2003) regarding Mozart biographers?

Biographers have become more reliant on Friedrich Rochlitz's stories.

answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that a trend noted in Stafford (2003) is for biographers to be less credulous, less sentimental, and more sensitive to information about Mozart's own society and times.
Incorrect. The article says biographers have become less credulous in believing Rochlitz, not more reliant on his stories.

Incorrect. The article does not say biographers have focused exclusively on Mozart's Vienna years.
